title: Update on MOE's Probe into Alleged Assault on Student at Admiralty Secondary School on 7 January 2025
what_it_is: Update on MOE's Probe into Alleged Assault on Student at Admiralty Secondary School on 7 January 2025

sections.label: Admiralty Secondary assault and bullying questions
sections.summary: An MP asked the Education Minister about investigations into an alleged assault at Admiralty Secondary School and a 2023 ex-student suicide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has conducted investigations into an alleged assault at Admiralty Secondary School on 7 January 2025; (b) if so, whether results of the investigations can be released; (c) whether any investigations have also been conducted on the suicide of an ex-student of Admiralty Secondary School in 2023, in particular, allegations that school leaders and the school principal dismissed the student's complaints about being bullied; and (d) whether any actions have been taken against perpetrators or school leaders involved in each case.

sections.label: Admiralty bullying rate and assault findings
sections.summary: MOE found about two bullying incidents yearly per 1,000 students, and the 7 January case was an altercation, not bullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For Admiralty Secondary School, in the last five years, there was an average of about two incidents of bullying per year per 1,000 students, both within and outside of school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Regarding the alleged assault case at Admiralty Secondary on 7 January, preliminary investigations by MOE reveal that it was not an incident of bullying, but an altercation that happened between two new Secondary 1 students during transition between periods.

sections.label: MOE stance and community partnership
sections.summary: MOE takes a firm stance against bullying and says parents and the community can partner teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: While MOE continues to take a firm stance against bullying, take care of our children and staff, help feuding parties to heal and guide our children in the proper ways, we – as parents and the wider community – can also partner our teachers and play our part by reminding ourselves of the following.

sections.label: Retributive and rehabilitative justice
sections.summary: The passage states that retributive justice must be coupled with rehabilitative justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Six, retributive justice must be coupled with rehabilitative justice.

sections.label: Few cases and low recidivism
sections.summary: The passage states these cases are few in schools and the recidivism rate is very low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As I have mentioned, these cases are few in our schools and the recidivism rate is also very low.
